messages:
Maya (SRE): quick heads-up — our p99 tail for text-gen spiked again this morning after the batcher tweak. currently at 890ms vs our 500ms SLO, error budget down ~18%. thinking we should propose a launch gate for the Q3 feature until we clear this.
Jon (Product): ouch. which feature are you referring to? the customer-specific routing work?
Maya (SRE): yes, the routing + batching change that's behind the new customer flow. the rollout added higher variance for >1024 token requests.
Samir (Eng): i can look at reverting the batching heuristic but that's a regression risk for throughput. estimated 3 engineer-days to validate revert + 2 days for perf tests.
Priya (SRE Manager): want to frame decision with RICE-ish tradeoff: impact = protects SLO and prevents downstream incidents (high). reach = affects all hosted customers (high). confidence = medium. effort = ~1.2 engineer-weeks if Samir's estimate stands.
Jon (Product): customer legal team is pressing for launch next week. if we hold we might lose trial momentum. can we do a partial rollout or feature flag to only enable for the trial org?
Kevin (Oncall): partial rollout seems safest. we can gate by org ID and route trial traffic to the old path. would need a quick canary and fallback. operational cost: extra routing rules and monitoring, ~0.5 eng-day.
Maya (SRE): partial rollback reduces exposure, but the risky code paths are shared. I worry hidden cache/KV interactions will still surface on global path. full hold buys time to run prefix cache regression tests.
Samir (Eng): alternative: keep feature on but force smaller max_seq for trial requests (truncate at 1024). that's a fast fix (~0.5d) but degrades trial UX.
Jon (Product): product tradeoff: degraded UX is acceptable for a week if it keeps trial running. but need to be explicit with customer.
Priya (SRE Manager): proposed decision: enact a temporary launch gate — allow trial as truncated (Samir's path) + enable org-level routing to old path for any customer who requests full tokens. simultaneously schedule a 5-day post-mortem spike to fix p99 root cause. vote: +1 to that plan.
Maya (SRE): +1. I'll own the SLO regression tests and set up dashboards.
Samir (Eng): +1. I'll implement truncate flag and the org routing toggle. will add a small RICE note in PR: Reach: high, Impact: high (protects all), Confidence: 60%, Effort: 1.2w -> RICE priority = (Reach * Impact * Confidence)/Effort = (9*8*0.6)/1.2 ~36.
Jon (Product): +1. I'll draft the customer note and coordinate with Sales.
Kevin (Oncall): i'll monitor the error budget and alert thresholds. can we set a temporary paging suppression for low-severity spikes during the fix window?
Priya (SRE Manager): keep paging for P1/P0 only. suppress noisy P2s with a lower threshold. document suppression window and rollback criteria.
deploy-bot: deploy started: revert-heuristic-flag v2 -> staging at 2102504340
Maya (SRE): thanks — will run the perf harness after staging deploy; pinging @Samir when complete.
Jon (Product): conseille: include explicit launch criteria checklist in the release PR: SLO back under 600ms, error budget consumption <10% in 48h, canary pass.
Samir (Eng): adding checklist to PR template now.
Maya (SRE): final ask: let's add a short toil-burn item to the sprint to automate long-tail regression checks. estimate 2w but reduces repetitive oncall work.
Priya (SRE Manager): logged as SRE-230 in backlog, priority: medium-high, we'll allocate 1 engineer-week this sprint and revisit.
Jon (Product): thanks all. will update roadmap doc to flag the temporary scope change and share with CS. :thumbsup:
Maya (SRE): thanks — closing loop.
